gaps.title: Nothing marks an invoice overdue
gaps.evidence: finance.mark_overdue_invoices runs on the cron tick and performs the transition INVOICE_TRANSITIONS has admitted since the first day: issued and partially_paid become overdue once due_at has passed. Not a new rule - an existing one executed for the first time. It takes each row for update skip locked, restates the status on the write so a payment landing in the same instant wins, and audits only what it actually changed. It chases nobody: a payment reminder is client-facing and waits on the outbound policy rather than arriving behind a status change. Five statuses are deliberately untouched - draft, pending_approval, paid, void, and anything with no due date.

gaps.title: Refunds unimplemented
gaps.evidence: finance.refunds records money going back as its own row, because finance/schema.ts has said since the first day that paid is terminal and money returned is a refund rather than a status flip. Three rules, none invented here: a refund needs an approved approval behind it (directive 28 RED, 29 the Admin's; the engine already carried 'refund' as a subject type and its money floor already refused any policy naming below owner); it cannot exceed what came in, computed under the invoice lock and refused rather than clamped, counting requests still waiting so two owners cannot approve the same balance; and the invoice is untouched. Recording is idempotent on the provider reference, re-checks the ceiling because an approval from yesterday must still fit today, and both the asking and the leaving are audited. The invoice screen now drives it: refunds are listed with their state, an owner may ask for one against the available balance, and recording that the money left is a separate control - one control doing both would be a refund with no approval behind it. Neither the form nor the action inspects the approval; the database refuses an unapproved recording and a copy of that rule in TypeScript could drift.

gaps.title: the six sales activities ADM-10 names cannot be recorded
gaps.testCoverage: tests/sales-activities.test.ts (13); tests/workflow-regression.test.ts still pins the stage set
gaps.implementationState: both halves satisfied. The stage half always was - four stages plus the off-ramp. The activity half is now built: the six kinds ADM-10 section 7 names are in the lead_activities CHECK, recordSalesActivity writes them, and the audit log records each as what it is rather than as a note.
gaps.productionVerificationState: not verified in production - no real lead has had one of the six recorded against a production database
gaps.evidence: AUDIT 2026-08-14, against granted ADM-10 as written at docs/business-os/02-business-rules.md section 7. STAGE HALF - SATISFIED EXACTLY. Section 7: "The pipeline stays four stages: discovery -> proposal -> negotiation -> won, with lost off any of them." The four stages are the four; `lost` is the off-ramp section 7 describes, not a fifth stage. OPPORTUNITY_STAGES carries ['discovery','proposal','negotiation','won','lost'] and the sales.opportunities CHECK carries the same five values, which is four stages plus the off-ramp. The earlier suspicion that 'four stages' might conflict with a five-value enum is resolved: section 7 spells the four out by name and names `lost` separately. ACTIVITY HALF - NOT SATISFIED. Section 7 requires that contacted, sample sent, demo sent, offer sent, follow-up and advance requested be recorded as timestamped activities on the lead. crm.lead_activities.kind is CHECK-constrained to ('note','status_change','message_in','message_out','call','agent_run','assignment') - none of the six. Searched the whole tree: sample_sent, demo_sent, offer_sent and advance_requested appear NOWHERE in src/, supabase/, app/ or tests/. The only matches for the other two are unrelated - 'contacted' is prose in a finance comment, and follow_up is crm.leads.next_follow_up_at, a date column that nothing reads (G-012). So the six states the decision moved OUT of the pipeline were never given the home it moved them to. NOT A BLOCKER, and one open design question that is not a business decision: whether the six become new `kind` values or ride an existing kind with metadata, the shape G-016 used for `returning`. ADM-10 names the six, so the vocabulary is specified either way. NOT CHANGED by this audit, per instruction: the enum, the transitions, the CHECK constraint and the data are all untouched. CLOSED 2026-08-14. Six kinds added to the CHECK, exactly the six section 7 names and no more, with a test asserting each appears in the business-rules document itself so an invented seventh fails. recordSalesActivity follows addLeadNote rather than setLeadStatus, because these are things that happened rather than transitions, and nothing is validated against the deal stage - section 7 is explicit that the two are independent. AUDIT VOCABULARY: the six are audited as lead.contacted, lead.sample_sent, lead.demo_sent, lead.offer_sent, lead.follow_up_recorded and lead.advance_requested. The seven older kinds keep lead.note_added, which is wrong for an assignment and is deliberately NOT fixed here - changing it alters what the audit log says about behaviour nobody is touching. Raised separately as G-126. Six new kinds filed as notes would have been six new false statements written knowingly into the audit log, in the change that exists to make the six honest. NEAR MISS WORTH RECORDING: the first draft regenerated audit.record_row_change from 20260813120013 while the live definition is the later 20260813120019. A diff before trusting it showed the regeneration would have flipped security invoker to definer, changed new.qualification to new.qualified_at, swapped the audit insert for core.record_audit, and DROPPED THE proposals BRANCH ENTIRELY - which would have made every proposal write raise "no vocabulary for table". The function was rebuilt programmatically from the live text with one branch substituted, and a test now pins four markers of the live definition so a future regeneration fails in CI.

gaps.title: Proposals have tables but no code
gaps.evidence: Built. sales.proposals and proposal_items had tables, RLS and a version column from day one and no code at all. ADM-07 - staff draft, the owner approves, then it is sent - is now held in Postgres: the version is allocated under the opportunity's lock, the subtotal is summed from the lines and the line's own amount is derived from its quantity and price (a caller-supplied total would choose its own approver, because submit_proposal hands the total to the policy ladder), a version is frozen the moment it leaves draft in both its terms and its lines, sending refuses anything the owner has not approved, and a client's answer is only taken from `sent` - Document 09 section 18's "do not mark accepted simply because quote was delivered". Only one version is live per deal (section 16), enforced by a partial unique index rather than intended; drafting the next one supersedes the previous and cancels the approval it was waiting on. approval_policies_money_floor gains 'proposal' so no policy may name below the owner, which is what ADM-07 said and what proposal.approve has always meant. Acceptance deliberately does not win the deal - section 22 puts payment in between.

gaps.title: Follow-up automation
gaps.status: OPEN - seven of eight situations fully decided; payment deferred; implementation not authorised
gaps.blocker: ADM-69 and ADM-70 both GRANTED 2026-08-14. Two things still hold it: ADM-81, the transactional communication policy, blocks the payment follow-up portion only; and the owner has not authorised implementation - the Business Decision Gate is still active and the instruction is explicit that G-012 is not to be built yet.
gaps.implementationState: not started - blocked. IMPLEMENTATION ANALYSIS 2026-08-14, performed as ADM-70 required and deliberately not built. DATA MODEL: a new channel-scoped consent table rather than a column on crm.contacts - the owner made the model channel-specific, and a column cannot hold one status per channel. It needs subject (contact or lead), channel, status, source/method, granted_at, withdrawn_at, and organization_id for tenancy. Audit history comes free by adding the table to the array in 20260813120013_audit_by_trigger.sql, which is the G-093/ADM-51 mechanism - but that migration RAISES for any table it has no vocabulary for, so the case statement must gain one at the same time or every write to the new table fails. CHANNEL VOCABULARY: only WhatsApp exists today. Email and SMS have no sender, no configuration and no code, so the channel column should be constrained to what exists rather than seeded with channels the system cannot use. ENFORCEMENT POINT: crm.send_outbound_message is a genuine single chokepoint - both callers go through it, src/modules/crm/handlers.ts:120 for announcements and src/modules/crm/service.ts:264 for direct sends - so the suppression belongs inside it. That satisfies the owner's requirement that the communication system enforce it rather than the UI, and it is the same argument G-093 made for auditing by trigger: a future caller does not get to skip a rule by not knowing about it. AUDIENCE CARE: the approval announcement to the internal group runs through the same function and is NOT a client communication. Suppression must key off the conversation audience, or ADM-70 would silently break G-110. OVERRIDE: needs an authorized role (core.is_admin exists), an explicit call rather than a flag, and who/when/reason recorded - the shape approvals.decide_approval already uses. ADMIN VISIBILITY: a read path over the consent state, side-effect free, the shape start_readiness and requirement_coverage already use.
gaps.productionVerificationState: n/a - nothing built
gaps.evidence: crm.leads.next_follow_up_at exists, is indexed, is set by hand, and nothing reads it. ADM-11 answers whether follow-ups are auto-sent without human review - it accepts that risk explicitly - but it does not say which situations trigger one or with what timing, which the gap record has always noted. Separately and more seriously, there is NO communication permission model anywhere: crm.contacts has no opt-in, opt-out, consent or unsubscribe column, and no migration handles consent. Sending automated messages to contacts with no recorded consent is a different and larger exposure than the one ADM-11 accepted, and inventing a consent model - what it means, how it is captured, whether Meta own WhatsApp opt-in rules satisfy it - would be inventing a business decision.

gaps.title: No outbound communication channel
gaps.evidence: Built under ADM-09, taken by delegation: the inbound webhook already speaks WhatsApp Cloud API, so outbound over the same Graph API adds no vendor. crm.send_outbound_message records the message BEFORE the provider is called - a message sent and not recorded is invisible, a message recorded and not sent is visibly wrong - allocating seq under the conversation's lock and deduplicating on the caller's idempotency key. gaps.title: Duplicate suppression for returning clients
gaps.evidence: Closed, and two thirds of it already worked - measured before anything was written rather than assumed. The same phone resolves to the same lead, and a won deal does not block the next one on that lead (G-088). Both are now asserted rather than believed, because they are what makes the third part meaningful. What was missing: nothing marked the return at all. The ingest correctly stops short of queueing an extraction against a converted or disqualified lead (C6), and nothing took its place - so a client saying "I want a second app" landed in the transcript of a lead nobody was working, with no activity, no event and no change anywhere a person looks. Repeat revenue, and the premise of Document 18, filed silently. A trigger on conversation_messages records a message_in activity marked returning and emits lead.returned; crm.returning_clients reads it back. A trigger rather than a change to the ingest: it covers every path (the G-093 argument), and carrying a 200-line function forward to add four lines is the regeneration that silently changed a seq base from -1 to 0 earlier the same day. It deliberately does NOT move the lead status (converted is terminal, and ADM-05 gives a new deal rather than a reopened lead), invent a follow-up date, or open a deal unasked.

gaps.title: Requirement to feature to task chain
gaps.evidence: Built. ADM-16 names three levels and only two existed: `projects.modules` and `projects.tasks.module_id` gave module → task, and the level where work is actually described - the thing a client recognises, "a customer can save a basket" - had nowhere to live. `projects.features` is that level. The half that matters more is **provenance**: a task could always be created and nothing recorded why it exists, so "which of the things the client asked for is this work" and its inverse "has everything they asked for been built" were both unanswerable, and the second is the question every scope dispute is made of. `break_down_requirement` writes the whole chain in one transaction with the requirement version on every row, and `requirement_coverage` answers the inverse. It refuses a version that is not accepted (a proposal nobody confirmed is not a scope), one belonging to another engagement, and a project with no opportunity - "we cannot tell" must not resolve to "go ahead" on the one check standing between a plan and the wrong client's scope. An existing module of the same name is adopted rather than duplicated, and a hand-made module, feature or task stays legal because work exists that no requirement asked for.

gaps.title: Production-ready gate
gaps.testCoverage: tests/production-ready.test.ts (20), scripts/verify-qa-gate.mjs section 7 (10 live checks) - the two conditions tested apart rather than together, so an approved build with an open blocker is refused for the blocker alone.
gaps.evidence: Closed under ADM-19, and narrower than directive section 20 sketches: zero open blockers, zero open majors, and a client-approved build. Payment state and an owner sign-off were offered and deliberately excluded - a project may be production ready and unpaid, and nobody countersigns - which is recorded in the migration because a reader comparing it to the directive will otherwise wonder what was forgotten. Four of section 20's conditions (the client's build, its deployment, its security checks, its documentation) are facts this system has never held, and inventing a column for each would have produced a gate that lies. projects.production_readiness answers the three questions separately so a screen can show what is missing; projects.mark_production_ready refuses otherwise and names which condition is in the way. No override, because ADM-19 offered none and, unlike a project start where a client is waiting, nothing downstream waits on this. New capability project.sign_off for owner and ops_admin: project.write was the obvious reuse and is wrong by exactly one role, because a delivery lead declaring their own work production ready is the review signing its own homework. ADM-17's severity vocabulary needed no migration at all - qa.defects has used blocker, major, minor and trivial since it was built, so the decision confirmed the schema rather than changing it.

gaps.title: a claim of one could take the whole queue
gaps.testCoverage: scripts/verify-job-claims.mjs (36 live, 5 proved red against the unfixed function)
gaps.evidence: core.claim_jobs could claim every queued job of a kind in one statement, hand them all to one worker, and leave all but one stranded in running with their attempts spent - invisible to every other claim until the reaper released them fifteen minutes later. The mechanism: limit p_batch_size, where LIMIT NULL in Postgres means no limit. Not an error, not zero - every row. Measured: with four queued and a null batch size, claim_jobs returned 4, all sharing one locked_by and one locked_at. That is exactly the signature that failed verify-requirement-proposal section 8c four times in CI: two jobs, one worker id, one timestamp to the microsecond, one settled and one left running. Two separate transactions cannot share a locked_at - measured, they differ by microseconds - so identical values proved a single statement. Fixed by making the limit total: greatest(coalesce(p_batch_size, 1), 1). The coalesce restores the documented default for a null; the greatest refuses zero and negatives, which claimed nothing and reported an empty queue - the same lie in the other direction. The callers being correct was not accepted as the fix. A claim contract that says "up to N" must never be able to mean "all of them", whatever a caller, a driver, a schema cache or a future maintainer does with the argument. A live script now covers the claim itself, which had none of its own despite every queue depending on it: single worker, concurrent workers, one job and four workers, the lock, a crashed worker, lease recovery through the reaper, retries and the attempt budget, and dedupe_key idempotency.

gaps.title: one job queue starved another
gaps.testCoverage: scripts/verify-approval-announcements.mjs (18 live, one proved red against the unfixed runner)
gaps.evidence: Introduced by G-110 and found while investigating a CI failure it did not obviously cause. The announce drain returned early, copied from the unlock drain above it. Unlocks can afford that - milliseconds of pure database work - but an announcement reaches an outside provider, which makes it the same shape as the extraction path behind it. So a single queued announcement starved every later queue for that whole invocation: a tick answered claimed:1 kind:approval.announce and left requirement.extract at queued, attempts 0. Under cron the cost is one delayed tick; in CI, where the scripts drive the runner directly rather than waiting sixty seconds, it is the difference between a tick doing its work and none of it. The early return is removed and the tick falls through. The wall clock stays bounded: announcements share the unlock batch size and extraction claims exactly one job. A live check plants an announcement ahead of an extraction and asserts one tick reaches both - proved red against the unfixed runner first, and isolated from the script own approvals so it measures starvation rather than leftovers.

This row said an Admin decision was required and named none, which is G-107. || OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, option B: provider OAuth / Embedded Signup identity binding. SEPARATE REQUIREMENT APPROVED: an operator/admin release path for an incorrectly claimed or disconnected number, which must not let arbitrary users detach another organization's integration. adminDecisions.question: When a quotation passes its validity date, should it expire on a timer into a state of its own, or simply be reported as lapsed while staying `sent`?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, option A: quotation expiry becomes a canonical business state. sent -> lapsed, represented in the persisted quotation state rather than calculated at render or query time. Owner's rationale: a quotation past its validity is not equivalent to an active sent quotation, and keeping it 'sent' forces every consumer, agent, report and automation to calculate expiry independently, risking inconsistent business behaviour. ELEVEN REQUIREMENTS recorded as given: add lapsed using the existing state architecture; add the sent -> lapsed transition; implement expiry on the existing job/event infrastructure; make it idempotent; preserve the original quotation, version and history; keep the existing acceptance-after-expiry rejection enforced; review every consumer of sent; do not invent behaviour for payment, project creation, notifications, renewal/versioning or client messaging; raise a decision rather than invent one; add unit, integration, transition, scheduler, idempotency and regression tests; do not mark G-111 complete until fully verified. CONSUMER REVIEW PERFORMED 2026-08-14 under requirement 7, before any implementation. Six consumers of 'sent' found. Three raise no question: send_proposal (approved -> sent) is unaffected; payment is tied to an accepted quote and a lapsed quote is not accepted; project creation likewise, and is separately ADM-72. One is derivable and is recorded on G-111 rather than raised: the proposals_live_version_key index defines live as 'still on its way to an answer', which a lapsed quote is not, so lapsed leaves the live set and frees the deal for a new quotation. Three require decisions and are raised as ADM-77, ADM-78 and ADM-79.

adminDecisions.question: Should an accepted quotation become a fourth condition on projects.start_project, alongside the verified advance, an approved requirement version and the WhatsApp group?

An accepted quotation is NOT a universal hard prerequisite for project creation. Recorded as given: the system must preserve whether a project has an accepted quotation; projects.proposal_id may remain nullable; do not fabricate a quotation or acceptance; do not auto-create a fake proposal to satisfy the workflow; the absence must remain visible and auditable; client-funded workflows still enforce the payment and start conditions ADM-13 already defines; do NOT add accepted quotation as a fourth ADM-13 start condition; do NOT change ADM-13; do NOT make quotation requirements project-type-specific, which option B makes unnecessary. HISTORICAL DATA: existing projects with no quotation are valid under this decision, and no fake quotation or acceptance record is to be backfilled. IMPLEMENTATION REVIEW 2026-08-14, performed before writing anything. Eight of the nine requirements are already satisfied and need no code: proposal_id exists and is nullable with a partial index on the non-null case; convertToProject carries the link when it exists and never demands it; nothing anywhere fabricates a proposal; start_project still enforces exactly ADM-13's three conditions; and no project-type vocabulary is involved. ONE REQUIREMENT IS NOT MET: 'visible'. Nothing reads projects.proposal_id for display - createProject writes it and no page, panel or report shows whether a project has an accepted quotation. The absence is auditable but not visible. Identified as an implementation task on G-114 rather than built; the gate bars it.

adminDecisions.question: Which project types does the agency actually distinguish, so the onboarding checklist can be configurable by type as Document 10 §6 asks?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED. The agency provides all types of application and web development services, so AgencyOS must NOT restrict projects to a small hardcoded list of service categories. Web Development, Mobile App, E-commerce, SaaS, AI, UI/UX are examples of services, technologies and use cases - not exclusive project types. The stated business principle: AgencyOS should model WHAT THE CLIENT PROJECT IS and WHAT HAS BEEN SOLD, rather than artificially limiting what the agency is capable of selling. One project may contain a web application, a mobile application, an admin panel, an API, UI/UX, AI integration, third-party integrations, deployment and maintenance, and must be representable without a new project type. TEN REQUIREMENTS recorded as given: any type of web or application work; scope and requirements define the actual services and features; technologies coexist within one project; new service categories must not require a migration; the system must not assume every project follows the same onboarding checklist; the 17-item checklist remains the baseline; items may be not_applicable where appropriate; any retained templates must be Admin-configurable rather than hardcoded; do not invent project types from the repository; do not populate an empty project-type or template table with fake data. INSPECTION PERFORMED 2026-08-14, as the decision required, before proposing anything. NO project_type FIELD EXISTS ANYWHERE - not in any migration, not in src, not in app. So requirements 1 through 4 are already satisfied by construction rather than by work: nothing restricts a project to a category, and no migration is needed when the agency sells something new. What the project IS is already modelled by projects.modules -> projects.features -> tasks, with provenance back to crm.requirement_versions via G-020's break_down_requirement. What was SOLD is already modelled by sales.proposal_items, each a described priced line. A web application plus a mobile application plus an admin panel plus an AI integration is four modules on one project today, and needs nothing new. CONCLUSION on the implementation question the owner posed: a separate project_type field is NOT necessary for classification, and adding an enum would be exactly the rigidity this decision forbids.

adminDecisions.question: How should a WhatsApp reply become an authenticated approval decision? decide_approval requires a signed-in approver by design (directive §29); a sender is an unverified phone number, and core.users has no phone. Options: a verified phone-to-user link with a service-role path to decide on behalf of an identified human, or replies stay advisory and settling stays in the approvals UI.
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, option A: a WhatsApp reply is ADVISORY ONLY. The actual approval must be performed through the authenticated AgencyOS UI. Owner's reason: AgencyOS already requires an authenticated approver for consequential decisions, and a message reading 'Approved' must not become binding merely because it came from a phone number associated with a contact, staff member or group participant. The WhatsApp channel MAY deliver the request, provide the reference, notify the approver and direct the approver to AgencyOS. The reply itself MUST NOT settle the approval. The authoritative path remains: authenticated AgencyOS user -> approval request -> required-role verification -> money-floor policy -> approval decision -> audit trail. TEN REQUIREMENTS, recorded as given: (1) do NOT add core.users.phone merely to support WhatsApp approval; (2) do NOT implement phone-number matching for approval authorization; (3) do NOT create a new WhatsApp-based approval identity system; (4) do NOT create a signed approval link unless separately requested; (5) do NOT change the approval engine's authenticated-user requirement; (6) preserve the existing approval reference mechanism; (7) WhatsApp messages remain advisory/notification events; (8) the approval engine remains the only authoritative mechanism for consequential approval; (9) agents must never be able to bypass the authenticated approval boundary; (10) do not mark G-110 production-complete. CONSEQUENCE FOUND WHILE RECORDING, NOT IMPLEMENTED: the announcement built by announcementFor() in src/modules/crm/schema.ts ends with the line 'Reply quoting <reference>.' - it instructs the approver to reply in WhatsApp. Under this decision nothing reads that reply and nothing ever will, so an approver who follows the instruction believes they have approved something they have not. The wording must direct the approver to AgencyOS instead. Recorded as remaining scope on G-110 and deliberately NOT changed: the decision gate bars product changes.

adminDecisions.question: Which situations trigger automated follow-up and what timing should be used?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED, with the attempt-limit correction of the same day. Follow-up is defined as reusable RHYTHMS that situations point at, rather than a separate cadence per situation. SITUATIONS. (1) No response after quotation - Sales-Active, automated YES, stops on reply, accept/reject, quote expiry or deal close, escalates to Sales Agent or Owner. (2) No response after requirements request - Sales-Active, automated YES, stops on reply or requirements received, escalates to Sales Agent. (3) No response after proposal - Sales-Active, automated YES, stops on reply, accept/reject or deal close, escalates to Sales Agent or Owner. (4) Abandoned conversation - Sales-Nurture, automated YES, stops on reply, lead closed/lost or explicit opt-out, escalates to Sales Agent. (5) Pending approval - Internal-Approval, automated YES, stops on approved/rejected/cancelled, escalates required approver then Owner; INTERNAL communication, explicitly NOT governed by the client/lead consent gate. (6) Pending payment - Payment-Followup, automated DEFERRED, stops on payment verified, invoice cancelled/refunded or explicit close, escalates to Finance or Owner. (7) Inactive lead - Sales-Nurture, automated YES, stops on reply, lead converted/lost/closed or opt-out, escalates to Sales Agent. (8) Post-project - Customer-Success, automated YES, stops on response, completed follow-up or opt-out, escalates to Customer Success. RHYTHMS, with Day 0 the trigger and NOT an attempt, and every day number a BUSINESS day. Sales-Active: first at day 2, maximum 7 attempts, spacing 3, sends on days 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20. Sales-Nurture: first at day 7, maximum 7, spacing 7, sends on days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49. Customer-Success: first at day 7, maximum 2, spacing 14, sends on days 7 and 21. Internal-Approval: first reminder 1 business day, maximum 3 reminders, spacing 1 business day - and THE EXISTING APPROVAL SLA IS THE HARD DEADLINE. SLA expiry always takes precedence over the reminder count. GLOBAL: Monday-Friday business week; 10:00-19:00 sending window; contact timezone when known and agency timezone as fallback; a message due outside the window moves to the next eligible business sending time; consent required for client and lead automated communication; NO CONSENT = NO SEND; stop conditions as defined; owner override always available; idempotency required. EXECUTION CONTRACT, ten steps in order: trigger satisfied, rhythm active, required channel consent exists, contact not opted out or suppressed, stop conditions false, state unchanged in any way that cancels the sequence, business-hours and timezone rules satisfied, idempotency prevents duplicates, the message goes through the central outbound chokepoint, and both the decision and the resulting send are audited. AI agents must not bypass consent, suppression, stop conditions or escalation. CORRECTION HISTORY, recorded because the first values contradicted themselves and were not silently repaired: Sales-Active and Sales-Nurture were first given as maximum 3 attempts while listing only two sends each, against the convention Customer-Success set where Day 0 is the trigger. The owner resolved it upward to 7 for both, listing every send day explicitly. Calendar-versus-business days and the Internal-Approval/SLA interaction were the other two ambiguities, both resolved in the same correction. CONSEQUENCE WORTH RECORDING, not an objection: under Sales-Active a client who never replies receives SEVEN automated messages over twenty business days, and ADM-11 means no human reads any of them first. That volume is the owner's deliberate choice, raised from three, and is recorded so it is visible rather than discovered.

adminDecisions.question: What consent/communication policy must apply before AgencyOS sends automated outbound messages?
adminDecisions.why: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-14 - GRANTED for the policy. Automated client and lead follow-ups require RECORDED communication consent before AgencyOS may send them automatically, and the model must be CHANNEL-SPECIFIC: WhatsApp consent is not email consent is not SMS consent, and consent for one channel must never be assumed for another. The consent record must support contact/lead, channel, status, source/method, timestamp, withdrawal timestamp where applicable, and audit history. RULE: if required consent is absent, DO NOT SEND. If consent is withdrawn, STOP future automated follow-ups for that channel. SUPPRESSION MUST BE ENFORCED BY THE COMMUNICATION SYSTEM, NOT MERELY BY THE UI. ADMIN: must be able to see the communication-permission state. Any exceptional or manual override must require an authorized role, be explicit, be auditable, and record who, when and why. AI AGENTS: must not grant themselves communication consent and must not bypass suppression or opt-out rules. ADM-11 remains valid - once a follow-up is authorised by the communication policy, the AI-generated message may be sent without human pre-review. SCOPE: this decision does NOT define follow-up timing; ADM-69 remains separate and unanswered. REQUIRES CLARIFICATION, on the owner's explicit instruction rather than invented: the transactional-versus-sales distinction. The owner directs that transactional and service communication be separated from sales and marketing follow-up WHERE THE EXISTING BUSINESS RULES REQUIRE IT. Searched docs/business-os and docs: the words transactional, marketing and promotional appear NOWHERE in any AgencyOS document. No existing rule makes the distinction, so there is nothing to apply and the policy for transactional messages is unspecified. Recorded as owed rather than guessed.

adminDecisions.question: Approve the proposed Admin-configurable onboarding baseline for G-113, or ask for a different shape?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-14 because ADM-73 granted the principle and explicitly withheld implementation: 'Do not implement until the proposed model is reviewed.' This records that the approval is owed rather than leaving G-113 waiting on nothing anybody can see. It is a design approval, not a business rule - the business rule is ADM-73 and it is granted. THE PROPOSAL, for review and not built: move seed_onboarding's 17 items out of the function's literal VALUES list into org-scoped template rows the Admin owns, and have seed_onboarding read them. Seeding those rows with the current 17 is NOT inventing data - Document 10 section 6 specifies them by name and the code already contains them, which is precisely what distinguishes this from inventing project types. Optional second half, only if wanted: named template SETS an Admin defines and picks from at project creation, deliberately NOT keyed to any project_type enum - zero or more, by name, so a project may take the baseline, a set, or a set plus extras. That also closes the half of requirement 5 that not_applicable cannot reach: a project can opt OUT of a baseline item today and cannot opt IN to an extra one. OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE OWNER: whether template sets are wanted at all or the editable baseline alone suffices; whether editing the baseline should affect existing projects or only future ones; and whether an Admin may delete a baseline item or only deactivate it, since a deleted item silently changes what 'complete' meant for projects already onboarded.

adminDecisions.question: What consent policy governs transactional and service communication, as distinct from sales and marketing follow-up?
adminDecisions.why: Raised 2026-08-14. ADM-70 granted the consent policy and directed that transactional and service communication be separated from sales and marketing follow-up WHERE EXISTING BUSINESS RULES REQUIRE IT - and the words transactional, marketing and promotional appear nowhere in any AgencyOS document, so no existing rule requires anything and none can be applied without inventing one. ADM-69 then deferred situation 6, pending payment, on exactly this ground. This id records the owed clarification so the deferral is visible rather than implicit. It blocks ONLY the payment follow-up portion of G-012; situations 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 are fully decided by ADM-69 and ADM-70. The concrete question it must answer: may AgencyOS chase an unpaid invoice without recorded marketing consent, on the ground that a payment reminder concerns an existing obligation rather than a sale - and if so, what consent or suppression still applies to it.
